_source: Every entry is read off the title page (or the imprint) of the edition named in its own `_source`, in ExternalFiles/000-Normes/ (docs/architecture/principles.md §2 rule 13, 11bis) -- never from memory and never from a handbook's restatement. An SIA title page prints its title in German, French, Italian and English and names its publisher in the language of the edition, so an SIA entry carries three titles and three publishers; a document whose edition exists in one language only carries one title, printed as it stands in every report (section 4bis: what no norm gives in a language is left as it is). ⚠️ Where the library does not hold the edition (the SIA documents the report templates cite and the library lacks, the VKF Brandschutznorm 1-15 and every German VKF directive), the entry's `_source` names instead the publisher's own page it was read off -- the title page of the preview PDF the SIA shop serves with the product (shop.sia.ch), or the cover of the directive on www.bsvonline.ch -- and says so with «Not in ExternalFiles/000-Normes/»; it is the same rule, read from the next most authoritative place.
_note: The documents the engine knows how to name in full, for the report's bibliography (`#show-bibliography`, lib/bibliography.typ). It is a **catalogue and not a list to print**: an entry is set only where the report actually cites it -- by the `norm` field of a record of the export, by a `norm:` argument of `#var`, `#eq`, `#val`, `#var-unit` or `#var-line`, or by `#cite-norm`. A project's own documents -- a manufacturer's ETA, an office handbook -- belong in that project's `references.bib`, not here. ⚠️ No entry names the file it was read from anywhere the report can print: the four fields a bibliography prints are the designation, the title, the edition and the publisher, which is the engineer's own list (v0.99). `_source` is for whoever checks the transcription.
